chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Mr. Young's talent and how his father understood him
summary: Lester's father had a legitimate tone and liked Cootie's playing; Cootie's father understood he wanted nothing but the trumpet.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Did you learn anything from him? From the father?
Well, what kind of tone did he get?
Yeah. I mean, he didn't have a feel for jazz, then, the father?
Oh, I see. Just the two boys, then, did. Did the girl?
Just Lester, I think. Mama could play and Lee could play.
Yeah. All of them could play.
Well, I'll be darned. Fancy that. That's extraordinary, isn't it?
Well, that's very interesting. Well that was -- so that was like good breaking in, for getting experience.
Yeah. Well that was good. So your father really did understand how you felt. He understood what's what with you, what you wanted.
I mean, he was in your corner.
It's very good. Well, okay. Well, let's go back.
